b2-145.title: A night at the observatory
b2-145.story: On Friday night, Anna and Max took a bus to the old observatory outside Kyiv. Under its dome, a guide let them look at the moon through a huge [[telescope]]. Anna was amazed to see a deep [[crater]] near its edge. The guide explained that a large [[asteroid]] had probably made it millions of years ago. "Out there, there's no air, only a [[vacuum]], so nothing slows the rocks down," she said. Suddenly, a bright [[meteor]] shot across the sky, and Max shouted with excitement. Later, the guide showed them a dark [[meteorite]] that had fallen in a nearby field. It still smelled faintly of [[sulfur]], like burnt matches. Anna's heart was racing, as if every nerve was sending an [[impulse]] straight to her brain. On the way home, the bright [[neon]] signs of the city looked boring compared to the stars.

b2-146.title: Strange mysteries
b2-146.story: On a rainy Saturday, Max's sister Sofia made everyone watch her favorite mystery show. The first episode claimed that a [[yeti]] had been filmed in the mountains, though the video was very blurry. In the next one, a man fell into a [[trance]] and said he could hear voices from the past. Then an old woman insisted that a [[demon]] lived in her attic, but it turned out to be a family of owls. Max joked that the host was probably a [[clone]], because he looked exactly the same in every episode. Anna pointed out a strange [[paradox]]: the less evidence there was, the more people seemed to believe. Sofia admitted that fear is a big [[factor]] in why these stories spread so fast. In the end, they all agreed that the owls were the best part of the show.

b2-147.title: Election day at school
b2-147.story: Anna's school held a mock election to show students how politics works. Ira was the [[candidate]] from Anna's class, and she called herself a proud [[democrat]] who believed every vote mattered. The school invited a retired [[senator]] from Poland, who was in Kyiv for a medical [[congress]], to speak to the students. He explained how his country's [[senate]] and lower house share power. Then he compared that system with the Ukrainian [[parliament]], which has only one chamber. After the talk, the students voted in a [[referendum]] on whether phones should be allowed at lunch. A loud group of boys, the so-called pizza [[lobby]], also campaigned for pizza every Friday. Anna's little brother Taras, who came to watch with Mama, said he wanted to be education [[minister]] one day and cancel all homework. In the end, the students reached a [[consensus]]: phones at lunch, but pizza only once a month. Ira won the election by six votes and promised to keep her word.

b2-148.title: A student world summit
b2-148.story: Anna and Max joined a Model UN [[summit]] at their university, where students played world leaders for a weekend. Anna was the [[delegate]] for Canada, and Max represented Brazil. Lisa, who dreams of becoming a [[diplomat]], helped them prepare their speeches the night before. On the first day, five small island nations formed an [[alliance]] to demand cleaner oceans. When the big countries ignored them, they announced a [[boycott]] of all trade talks. Then a young [[activist]] from a local environmental group gave a powerful talk about plastic in the Black Sea. Max, a proud [[patriot]], kept mentioning Ukraine even though he was supposed to speak for Brazil. The organizers laughed and said his [[patriotism]] was admirable but against the rules. By Sunday, everyone had signed a short ocean agreement, and they celebrated with pizza.

b2-149.title: Ideas that divide
b2-149.story: For her history project, Anna called her grandparents to ask about life in the past. Grandpa said that Ukraine lived under Soviet [[communism]] when he was young, and shops often had empty shelves. His own father had been a [[communist]], mostly because joining the party helped him keep his job. When Anna asked about [[socialism]], Grandpa explained that many European countries mix some of its ideas with a free market. "Grandma's cousin in Sweden calls himself a [[socialist]], yet he runs his own bakery, so maybe he's secretly a [[capitalist]]," he laughed. Then Grandma took the phone and talked about [[feminism]] and how women fought for equal pay. She had been a proud [[feminist]] long before the word reached their village, because she saw so much [[sexism]] at her factory. Finally, Anna asked about [[racism]], and Grandpa's voice became serious. "A [[racist]] judges people before knowing them, and that's just lazy thinking," he said. Anna got the best grade in her class, and she sent her grandparents a photo of it.

b2-150.title: Army life on a film set
b2-150.story: Max's sister Sofia got a small role as an extra in a historical war film, and she invited Max and Anna to watch the filming. The set was a muddy field outside Kyiv, where a [[bulldozer]] had dug long trenches the week before. An actor playing a young [[lieutenant]] kept forgetting his lines, which made the director sigh loudly. The [[sergeant]], played by a much older actor, quietly helped him remember them. Sofia, dressed in green [[camouflage]], had to hide behind a fake [[bunker]] made of painted foam. In the main scene, a [[sniper]] on a rooftop was supposed to spot the enemy and warn everyone. Then came a pretend air [[raid]], with loud sound effects and clouds of smoke. The special effects team used a tiny, carefully controlled amount of [[dynamite]] to blow up an old wooden barn. After ten takes, the director finally shouted "Perfect!" and Sofia's part was over. On the way home, she admitted that her favorite part of the day was the free lunch.

b2-151.title: Faith and belief
b2-151.story: This semester, Anna's university group did a project on world religions. A classmate from Turkey explained the basics of [[Islam]] and invited everyone to an evening meal during [[Ramadan]]. Lisa, a [[Catholic]] from Lviv, talked about Christmas traditions in her grandmother's village. Ira interviewed a [[pastor]] at a small church near campus, who told funny stories about the weddings he had led. Max, who calls himself an [[atheist]], was surprised by how much he enjoyed the interviews. Anna chose [[Buddhism]] and visited a [[Buddhist]] teacher who runs a quiet meditation center in Podil. He explained that [[karma]] means your actions come back to you, whether they are good or bad. Every morning, he sits in silence for twenty minutes, a simple [[ritual]] that calms his mind. At the final presentation, the group agreed that every faith they studied valued kindness. Then they all went to their classmate's home for dinner, and Max ate more than anyone.

b2-152.title: Warriors of the past
b2-152.story: Last weekend, Anna took her little brother Taras to a history festival in an old [[fort]] outside Kyiv. Actors in costumes were showing how warriors from different times lived and fought. Taras couldn't take his eyes off a [[samurai]] in shiny armor who explained how he cared for his sword. Nearby, a muscular [[gladiator]] invited children to try lifting his heavy shield. At noon, two knights fought a [[duel]] with wooden swords, and the crowd cheered for both of them. In a big tent, a woman dressed as a [[nomad]] from the steppes showed how her people packed their homes onto horses. Suddenly, a masked [[bandit]] ran through the crowd and grabbed Taras's hat, but it was just part of the show. The actor returned the hat with a small wooden [[talisman]] as an apology. Taras has worn it around his neck every day since, saying it keeps monsters away.
